newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex sees 1996/97 net up strongly.
newsitem.headline: Vendex sees 1996/97 net up strongly.

text.p: Retail and business services group Vendex International NV said on Tuesday it expected its 1996/97 net profit to show a strong rise compared to the previous financial year, when it booked a net profit of 415 million guilders.
"The profit per ordinary share will rise significantly," Vendex said in a statement.
It said operating profits excluding real estate income would also show strong growth, adding that all five divisions were expected to contribute to the increase.
Vendex said net group turnover increased by some eight percent to 12.1 billion guilders in 1996/97.
Retail turnover rose by nearly six percent, while business services booked a turnover growth of almost 15 percent, it said.
"The increase in retail turnover was generated by organic growth, continued expansion and acquisitions," Vendex said.
It added the food retail division raised its turnover by 3.4 percent, gaining some market share in the Netherlands.
Vendex said losses at its Belgian food retail business had been cut significantly compared with last year as a result of previous restructurings.

"After the recovery in consumer spending during the second quarter, turnover in the non-food retail business developed in line with expectations, notably during the important last quarter," Vendex said.

In 1996/97 Vendex's department stores realised a turnover increase of more than four percent, the first rise in many years. Sales at the group's specialty stores grew more than 14 percent, which was partly due to acquisitions.
"In most segments, market shares again increased," Vendex said.

Within the businesses services division, turnover at the temporary employment subsidiaries increased by 16 percent, in spite of a six percent decline in the French market for temporary employment, Vendex said.
Vendex said the growth in this sector was mainly realised in the Netherlands and Belgium, partly through acquisitions.
The maintenance services unit increased its turnover by about 13 percent, mainly because of the consolidation of a French takeover in 1995, Vendex said.

The group said the number of stores it operated grew to 1,969 from 1,732, while the number of temporary employment offices, excluding the 104 outlets of Vendex's participation in Spanish firm Laborman, increased to 588 from 536.
